title: Nike Stock Plunges 8.5% After Revenue Miss, Steep Forecast Cut and Job-Cut Plan
excerpt: Nike reported $11.21 billion in quarterly revenue, below Wall Street estimates, and warned full-year revenue will decline by a high single-digit percentage — unveiling a 'Pace' restructuring with job cuts and a new India campus.
body:
• Nike shares fell 8.5% in extended trading after the company reported weaker-than-expected quarterly revenue and a steep full-year forecast cut.
  • Fiscal first-quarter revenue came in at $11.21 billion, down 4%, versus Wall Street's $11.32 billion expectation; Greater China sales fell 26% on a constant-currency basis.
  • The company unveiled "Pace," an operating-model overhaul promising $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031 — including job cuts and a new campus in India.
  • CEO Elliott Hill, nearly two years into his turnaround, admitted reviving sportswear, Jordan brand and Greater China "will take time."

Nike's comeback story just got a lot more painful. The sportswear giant's shares sank 8.5% in extended trading on Thursday after it reported first-quarter revenue that missed analysts' estimates and slashed its full-year outlook, while unveiling a restructuring plan that will eliminate jobs and include a new campus in India.

Fiscal first-quarter revenue was $11.21 billion, down 4% from a year earlier and below the $11.32 billion Wall Street expected, according to reports. Diluted earnings were $0.48 a share, while gross margin improved 60 basis points to 42.8%, helped by lower warehousing and logistics costs. But the market focused on the outlook: Nike now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to decline by a high single-digit percentage, far worse than the roughly 2% decline analysts had pencilled in. Adjusted earnings were forecast at $1.15 to $1.35 a share.

Context & Background

The earnings deepened investor frustration with CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround, nearly two years into his tenure. The company has been refocusing on key sports such as running and rebuilding relationships with wholesale retailers, but Greater China sales tumbled 26% on a currency-neutral basis in the quarter, and several lifestyle franchises remain under pressure.

"Our Nike performance business is not yet large enough to offset the pressure we're seeing in Nike sportswear, Jordan brand, and Greater China."

— Elliott Hill, Nike CEO

Analysts say the company's struggles partly reflect a failure to release enough compelling new products, forcing a rise in promotions and discounts. CFRA analyst Zach Warring told Yahoo Finance the quarter was "a quarter you'd expect from a new CEO three or four quarters in, but not two years in" — a sign expectations are being reset lower rather than the business returning to growth.

Impact & Analysis

Nike announced "Pace," an overhaul of its operating model extending its Sport Offence strategy across the company, which it expects to generate about $2.5 billion in cumulative savings through fiscal 2031. The programme includes supply-chain modernisation, organisational streamlining, consolidation from four geographic divisions to three — Americas, Asia Pacific and Greater China, and EMEA — and job cuts whose number the company says it does not yet know, with employee notifications beginning in 2027.

The restructuring is a recognition that the turnaround will take several more quarters at least. Nike also said it would deliberately reduce the volume of Jordan retro launches, a franchise that has been central to its lifestyle weakness.

Diaspora Angle

The announcement of a new Nike campus in India "with strong capabilities and access to talent" is the detail Indian observers will watch most closely — it signals where the world's biggest sportswear brand sees its next pool of designers, engineers and supply-chain talent, even as it cuts roles elsewhere.

What's Next

Nike begins the Pace rollout this fiscal year, with job notifications starting in 2027. Investors will be watching the next two quarters for any stabilisation in China and evidence that new product launches can lift the lifestyle franchises out of their slump.
